newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INL says not able to seal Sky TV deal.
newsitem.headline: INL says not able to seal Sky TV deal.

text.p: Independent Newspapers Ltd said on Friday that negotiations for the purchase of a shareholding in pay TV operator Sky Network Television were at an end, and it had regrettably not been possible to structure an agreement which would have been satisfactory to all the parties involved.

"The board of INL came to the view that it was no longer possible to pursue the transaction in the form proposed, despite the best efforts of all those involved," INL Managing Director Michael Robson said in a statement.

Robson said the INL board was disappointed by not being able to complete the deal. A number of issues had not been able to be resolved. However, he said these issues did not involve Television New Zealand, which had been an enthusiastic potential partner of INL and had assisted INL during the negotiations.
Robson added that INL believed Sky was a good company and admired the progress it had made in establishing itself over a short period of time.
INL would be keen to look at any opportunities to develop business associations with Sky that may arise in the future.
Robson said he was certain that the move to multi-channel digital satellite transmission would be successful.
INL first announced it was negotiation to purchase a shareholding in Sky at its annual meeting in October last year.
At the that time INL said it was negotiating with a group of companies that together own more than 80 percent of Sky to buy a substantial stake.

Those companies included Heatley Jarvis Investments (15.8 percent), Todd Corporation (8.8 percent), Tappenden Construction (7.7 percent) and United States-based HKP Partners (51.1 percent). HKP is partly owned by Bell Atlantic and Ameritech, which in turn own half of Telecom Corp of New Zealand.
State-owned Television New Zealand holds the remaining 16.4 percent of Sky and reportedly wanted to raise its stake to about 25 percent.
INL is just under half-owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation. Sky is not related to Murdoch's 40 percent-owned European-based satellite network BSkyB.
